decisions.reason: As a 2023 launch on the home page that is close to the firm's core dosimetry and QA business, it carries high visible commitment and strong strategic fit, so management is very unlikely to withdraw it quickly.

This software extends the firm's established oncology QA offering and supports its stated direction toward integration, automation, and prediction, which makes management inclined to continue backing it despite any early uncertainty.
The CT phantom is a recent launch within the firm's existing medical imaging QA domain, so sunk development effort and the normal expectation of a ramp-up period favor keeping it on the market.

Although this mammography phantom is more distant from the core offer, it was publicly launched only in 2024 and an escalating management team would usually give such a new adjacent product more time before admitting retreat.

This product is also peripheral to the firm's main radiation therapy focus and therefore more vulnerable, but its recent launch and explicit market presentation still make continued commitment more likely than an immediate withdrawal.
A multi-model imaging QA instrument line implies substantial investment and signals a broader portfolio move consistent with the firm's expansion, so management is likely to persist with it.
